content:
Two contradictory reports appeared yesterday about next year's iPhone model, which is set to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone's launch and is said to embody Apple's long-standing vision of "a single piece of glass."

Reports on what we can actually expect have been all over the place for some time, but yesterday's divergence was arguably the starkest yet...

Current situation

Apple's former design chief, Jony Ive, frequently spoke of his long-term vision of eventually making the iPhone a single slab of glass; even with Ive gone, the general belief is that Apple is still heading in this direction.

While Apple doesn't generally make a big deal of anniversaries, the consensus in the industry is that they are aiming to get as close to this vision as possible for the iPhone's 20th anniversary. This would very likely include embedding Face ID under the display and hiding the front-facing camera beneath the screen as well.

However, we've already seen contradictory reports on these expectations. The initial view was that this would be a standalone model, similar to the iPhone Air and the upcoming iPhone Ultra, but more recent reports have pointed to this design appearing on next year's iPhone Pro models.

In sequence, that would be the iPhone 19 Pro, though Apple might also want to skip a generation and name it the iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary.

Yesterday's contradictory reports

Yesterday's situation became even more muddled when an analyst claimed Apple had scrapped the idea of an all-glass iPhone next year.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman quickly pushed back against this claim.

The more likely reality

The point is that Apple's vision for the iPhone doesn't have a single endpoint. What they plan to deliver next year is just one or several steps toward that sci-fi vision of "a single piece of glass."

The question isn't whether this goal can be achieved next year, but how many steps Apple will take toward it. But whether it's one step or several, this certainly won't be the final step in the iPhone's design evolution.

In fact, Gurman revealed that Apple has actually pulled back somewhat from what it originally hoped to achieve next year.

The Jefferies analyst likely heard the same news, but was a step behind and mistakenly thought the plan had been entirely abandoned.

My own expectation is that next year's design will be a major leap forward—comparable to the breakthrough of the iPhone X—but there will be further developments in the years after. For me, the biggest question is whether the 2027 iPhone will have a big enough leap to warrant some sort of special branding, such as marking it as a 20th anniversary iPhone edition (which I think is extremely unlikely), giving it another special name, or skipping a generation to call it the iPhone 20.

What are your hopes? Share them in the comments.
